title: SCIM: async deprovision rollback and orphan membership reconciliation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our SCIM provisioning pipeline intermittently leaves 'orphaned' group memberships when deprovision requests fail or are retried out-of-order. This shows up after identity provider retries and transient network errors: users exist but group edges are stale, or users are soft-deleted while a later successful provisioning event re-creates partial state. This causes permission drift under RBAC v2 and noisy audit trails for customers.

Goal: Implement an asynchronous rollback and reconciliation mechanism for SCIM provisioning that: 1) makes user/group create/update/delete idempotent across retries, 2) detects and repairs orphaned membership edges without blocking realtime provisioning, 3) surfaces clear audit logs and admin controls to approve or reverse automated fixes. The solution must minimize customer-visible disruptions and provide metrics/alerts for any non-repairable cases.
acceptance_criteria: Provisioning requests include a stable transaction id (X-SCIM-TX) and retries use the same id; system deduplicates based on transaction id
Async rollback path implemented so that failed partial deprovision operations are retried or rolled back without manual intervention for >= 99.5% of incidents
Orphan membership detector runs as a background job and repairs membership mismatches within 15 minutes for 95% of cases
All automated fixes generate structured audit log entries correlating original SCIM event id, detected discrepancy, repair action, and acting service/principal
Admins can view pending automated repairs and approve/abort from Console (Requires Console change: Pending SCIM Repairs panel)
New metrics published: scim.tx.dedup.rate, scim.orphan.detect.count, scim.orphan.repair.success_rate, scim.rollback.latency
End-to-end integration tests for idempotency, out-of-order retries, and membership reconciliation added to CI
implementation_notes: API: accept X-SCIM-TX header; if absent generate transaction id but log for audit. Transaction id is the canonical dedup key for 72h
Provisioning runtime to record ProvisioningEvents with schema: tx_id, scim_id, op_type, affected_principals, status, last_seen_ts (flat string fields recorded in DB rows)
Add a lightweight 'membership expected state' watermark per group (sequence number) to detect stale edges cheaply before doing full diff
Async rollback worker: scans ProvisioningEvents for ops in 'partial-failure' state, and attempts compensating actions. Backoff strategy: exponential with jitter up to 10m, then escalate to DLQ
DLQ: dead-letter queue entries must include human-readable reason + original SCIM payload + suggested admin actions. DLQ entries surface in Console and emit PagerDuty if count > 5/min for a customer

Orphan detector: bucketed job that compares group membership snapshots against latest 'expected state' derived from idempotent SCIM events; repairs performed as separate transactions with their own tx_id and audit log reference
Idempotency: all membership modifications use an idempotency token derived from the tx_id + target_edge tuple to avoid double application
Audit logging: structured JSON lines to internal audit stream (s3/kafka). Fields: tx_id, event_id, scim_op, actor, target_type (user/group/membership), delta, outcome, repair_ref
Console: add 'Pending SCIM Repairs' view with filters (customer, severity, age) and 'Approve/Reject' actions that bind to repair jobs
Security: repair workers run with least privilege service principal and operations are recorded as 'system:scim-repair' in audit logs
SLOs: provisioning success >= 99.9% over 30d, orphan repair success >= 99.5% over 30d. Track regressions in SLO alerting

Add a feature flag to gate background repairs so we can opt-in customers for initial rollout
